pr.title: Plan incremental reviews of minimal pushes
pr.head: f1747437c980caf556dd7c5c4cd4e92dd546e4d8

summary: Projector's review loop watches the operator's pull requests and runs a full review on every head pushed to them. A full review reads every changed file, runs the repository's tests and checks, and posts a verdict whose body restates the change's intent and what it checked. A verdict is the review's outcome, clean or changes requested, and on your own pull request the loop also marks it ready or draft to match.

A full review costs the same whether the push is a large rewrite or a one-pixel padding fix. On #209, eight of 18 verdicts followed pushes that changed only a stylesheet by 15 lines or fewer, and those eight reviews took 638 seconds.

This pull request adds one plan, at status: ready and priority: next, and changes no code. The plan lets the loop post an incremental review: a short clean verdict on a head whose change since the loop's last full review the reviewer has read in full and judged to need nothing more.

1. A new command measures the change. project review interdiff finds the loop's last full review and replays that head's change onto the new merge base with git merge-tree. A pushed commit, a merge of the base, a rebase, and an amend all measure the same way, and a resolved conflict shows against both sides. The command also checks the rules that need no judgment, including a passing gate when the merge base moved.
  2. The reviewer decides. The subagent reads every line and asks whether the full method would catch something the read cannot. Prose is also read for accuracy and against the comment rules.
  3. Publish posts the review. project review publish --incremental --body <file> rechecks the rules and posts a clean comment with the usual review marker, a new projector-incremental marker line, a lead that links the full review, and the reviewer's few sentences.

cards.title: Review history
cards.html:
• 8c0196e: changes requested with two findings. A prose edit carried on its kind alone, with no accuracy check, and a clean base merge carried with no gate run.
  • f174743: clean. § 2.2.2 now reads prose for accuracy and against guidelines.md § 1, and § 2.2.1 requires a passing gate when the merge base moved. The plan also moved to incremental-review and replaced the line limit with the reviewer's judgment.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Incremental review: a clean verdict on a new head that rests on the loop's clean full review of an earlier head plus a read of the change since.
  • Interdiff: the change to the pull request's own diff between the full review's head O and the new head N, with what the base brought in left out.
  • MO and MN: the merge bases of O and N with the base branch.
  • Gate: the repository's validation commands, which project review gate runs on a trusted head.

groups.title: The incremental review plan
groups.kicker: The rules an incremental review must pass, how the change is measured, and what the review says
intro: The plan splits the decision in two. Code checks what a read of the patch cannot see: whether a loop runs the review, whether the head is trusted, whether this loop's clean full review precedes it with the same version, model, and effort, whether a finding is open, whether the change can be measured and read, and whether the gate passed when the merge base moved. The reviewer then reads every line and decides.

The change is always measured from the last full review, never from the previous incremental one, so a chain of small pushes is read together. The incremental review keeps today's review marker unchanged and adds its own marker line, so every existing reader of verdicts keeps working.

checks.text: The plan is at status: ready, which claims that every question blocking implementation is answered or deliberately deferred. § 6 defers a list of always-full-review paths and an incremental review that requests changes.

files.note: The whole plan: the problem on #209, the design, its reasons, acceptance criteria, cost, deferred questions, and the code facts it rests on.

checks.text: The #209 figures match GitHub: the pull request has 18 Projector verdicts, the eight review times in § 7 sum to 638 seconds, and git diff --shortstat gives the table's counts for the heads checked.
Checked in src/projector/review.py: gate writes the command's exit_code and the head's sha to the review's state, so this rule can read the record rather than the reviewer's word.
This paragraph answers the first review's finding: a prose hunk qualifies only when it is accurate against the code and a comment passes guidelines.md § 1.
Run in a scratch repository: this command exits 1 on a conflicting replay, writes a tree whose diff3 markers carry the full SHAs of MN, MO, and O, and lists the conflicted path after the tree id.

Why MO comes from the loop's record: after a stack's parent is amended and the child rebased, git merge-base O MN falls below the parent's old commits, and the replay would bring them along as false conflicts.

Retargeting a stacked child onto main after its parent merges also moves the merge base without a merge, so this label and the lead's "across a merge" would misdescribe that head. The review lists this as a suggestion.

A checkout that was never installed reports its version as unknown, so the same-version rule alone does not guarantee a record entry has base. The review suggests saying that an entry without one refuses as unmeasurable.
